plan.title: pan handoff has no --project: an isolated --cwd lands every successor outside all registered projects (conv 1827)
plan.author: agent:k3[1m]

references.label: PAN-1577 (shares the project_key column this plan creates)

metadata.sizeJustification: One mechanism (the project_key column) threaded through exactly the surfaces the issue's acceptance criteria name: the conversations door, the shared fork route, both CLI verbs that reach it, the three grouping surfaces the ACs require (deck, sidebar, palette), the modal the ACs require, the mandated data cleanup, and the mandated docs. The file count is driven by the repo's own door separation (one-to-five-line edits per file), not by scope creep; the items are vertically interlocked (WI-2..8 are meaningless without WI-1's column) and cannot ship independently as sibling issues without each being unreviewable alone. No item can be dropped without leaving a named AC unmet (palette routing is a grouping surface under the 'grouping honours the explicit association first' AC).

narratives.Problem: pan handoff has no way to declare the successor conversation's project. Grouping is pure cwd containment, and the universal isolated---cwd rule guarantees an isolated handoff cwd is outside every registered project path, so every correctly-isolated handoff lands in the No-project bucket by construction (live repro: conv 1827 doing MYN work from /home/eltmon/Projects/hoff-agent-surface).
narratives.Proposal: Add one explicit association primitive — a nullable project_key column (projects.yaml key) on the conversations row, written only through the conversations door — and thread it through: (1) schema top-up + door support + setConversationProjectKey writer (the same primitive PAN-1577's move UX will reuse); (2) the summary-fork route accepts an optional projectKey (yaml key or display name, 400 on unknown) and otherwise stores the SOURCE conversation's effective project on the successor, never re-deriving from the successor's cwd; (3) pan handoff and pan fork gain --project; (4) all grouping surfaces (projectsData helper, CommandDeck partition + resolveConversationProjectName, palette routing) resolve explicit-first and fall back to cwd containment; (5) the Fork/Handoff modal gains a Project select defaulted to 'Same as source'; (6) POST /api/conversations stores the key it already validates; (7) conv 1827 is reassigned to mind-your-now through the write door. Full detail in the PRD draft (.pan/drafts/PAN-3419.md).
narratives.NonGoals:
- No move-conversation UX (endpoint, pan conv move, drag-and-drop, menu action, UI clearing) — PAN-1577, which reuses this column and writer.
- No 'No project' option in the modal select (deliberate un-scoping is a move/clear operation).
- No fork-blob (ForkRequest) project field — the row carries the association; recovery re-runs against the existing row.
- No backfill beyond conv 1827 — existing rows keep NULL and cwd-derived grouping.
- No change to workspace_id or workspace-keyed memory attribution.
- No change to frontend cwd-containment match order (no longest-prefix rework); only the explicit-first step is added.

autoDecisions.summary: One mechanism shared with PAN-1577: nullable project_key TEXT column on conversations (yaml key) + setConversationProjectKey writer in the door.
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-1577 (open) already leans toward an explicit projectKey override column so JSONL is never relocated; the issue demands one mechanism, and a plain nullable column is the smallest primitive satisfying both. Reusing workspace_id was rejected: it is cwd-derived state, changing it would silently reroute workspace-keyed memory, and grouping would need a workspace→project join the frontend cannot do.

autoDecisions.summary: Store the yaml key; accept key-or-name on input via new resolveRegisteredProjectKey, which does NOT require the project path to exist.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks to match POST /api/conversations' acceptance rule (resolveProjectCwd accepts key or display name). Path existence is a cwd-usability requirement, not an association requirement — the successor's cwd is independent of the project path. Unknown input still fails loudly.

The blob exists so recoverStuckForks can re-run the pipeline for an already-created row; the association is persisted on the row at createConversation time, before the pipeline starts, so recovery never consults the blob for it. Adding it would be dead weight (simplicity-first).

autoDecisions.summary: pan fork gains --project too, and inheritance applies to all fork modes server-side.
autoDecisions.rationale: Same route, same defect class: an isolated-cwd pan fork misfiles identically. The CLI delta is one .option line plus pass-through; the server inheritance lives in the shared handler.

autoDecisions.summary: POST /api/conversations stores project_key when projectKey is given.
autoDecisions.rationale: It already validates and cwd-resolves the value; storing it makes the association explicit from birth instead of relying on containment forever. Same mechanism, one extra argument.

autoDecisions.summary: Modal default 'Same as source' sends no projectKey; no explicit 'No project' option.
autoDecisions.rationale: Omission already means inherit server-side, so the default needs no wire value. Deliberate un-scoping is a clear/move operation that belongs to PAN-1577's UX, not this issue.

autoDecisions.summary: Stale/unknown stored project_key values fall back to cwd containment at grouping time.
autoDecisions.rationale: A stored key whose project was later unregistered must not strand the conversation in a phantom group; cwd containment is the existing, understood fallback (NFR-1 preserved).

autoDecisions.summary: Conv 1827 cleanup runs pre-merge through a bun -e door invocation from the workspace.
autoDecisions.rationale: Opening overdeck.db via getOverdeckDatabaseSync applies the WI-1 top-up idempotently, and the old server's explicit-column INSERTs ignore the extra nullable column, so the write is safe against the live DB. It satisfies 'through the write door' without building PAN-1577's move endpoint early.

narrative.Action: Foundation for the whole issue — exact edits are specified in PRD WI-1 (.pan/drafts/PAN-3419.md). (a) infra.ts: add runSchemaTopUp(db, 'ALTER TABLE `conversations` ADD COLUMN `project_key` text') after the workspace_id top-up (line 277). (b) conversations.ts: add project_key to LegacyConversationRow, LEGACY_CONVERSATION_SELECT, LegacyConversation (projectKey), rowToLegacyConversation; createConversation accepts projectKey?: string | null and inserts it (never derived at write time); add exported setConversationProjectKey(name, projectKey | null) writer. This file is over the 1000-line ratchet — add a scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt row '<new-count> src/lib/overdeck/conversations.ts # PAN-3419'. (c) projects.ts: add resolveProjectKeyForCwd(cwd) — longest-prefix containment over listProjectsSync paths, returns yaml key or null (exact snippet in PRD). (d) conversation-runtime.ts: add resolveRegisteredProjectKey(input) — key-or-display-name match returning the canonical yaml key, 'Unknown project: <input>' error otherwise, NO path-existence requirement (exact snippet in PRD); in handleConversationCreate, when projectKey is present, validate via resolveRegisteredProjectKey (400 on error) before the existing resolveProjectCwd check, and pass projectKey: keyResult.key into createConversation. (e) New test file src/lib/overdeck/__tests__/conversation-project-key.test.ts following the OVERDECK_HOME-fixture pattern of conversation-project-cwd.test.ts (set process.env.OVERDECK_HOME to a tmp dir before the first dynamic import; projects.yaml fixture with a key≠name project and nested paths).
